# Proposal

The purpose of this project is to characterize the impact of Cks1/2 depletion on the proteome and transcriptome. Two human cell lines (HeLa and RPE1) were treated with either non-targeting siRNA, or siRNA targeting Cks1/2. Samples were then sent for RNAseq (Novogene) and MS-based proteomics (FingerPrints) analysis. Illumina paired end sequencing on polyA+ selected mRNAs was performed. There are 16 raw sequence read files. Matched samples are in the queue for proteomics analysis. We would like assistance

 1. mapping RNAseq reads and differential expression analysis,
 2. normalizing and comparing proteomics data to RNAseq,
 3. generating a web/html-based resource to visualize these datasets.



# Sequencing and mapping

@tbl-software lists the software tools used for the cleaning, quality control, and mapping of FASTQ files. These operations were conducted on the Life Sciences cluster utilizing a [snakemake](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bartongroup/MG_Cks12/main/rna_seq/Snakefile?token=GHSAT0AAAAAACML2LJKPBONK2PV7GSTPJOQZQC2CFA) script. Subsequently, the data were imported into RStudio and further processed using R.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-software
#| tbl-cap: Software used for cleaning, quality control and mapping FASTQ files.
tibble::tribble(
  ~Software, ~Version, ~Purpose,
  "Trim Galore!", "0.6.10", "Trimming adapters",
  "RiboDetector", "0.3.1", "Removing ribosomal contamination",
  "FastQC", "0.12.1", "Quality control",
  "FastQ Screen", "0.15.3", "Checking sample contamination",
  "STAR", "2.7.11a", "Mapping"
) |> 
  gt()
```

## Sequencing

Sequencing was done by NovoGene. 

## Ribosomal RNA removal

A tool [RiboDetector](https://github.com/hzi-bifo/RiboDetector) was used to remove reads matching ribosomal RNA from FASTQ files. RiboDetector is a machine learning tool that can recognize ribosomal RNA. @fig-ribo illustrates ...


```{r}
#| label: fig-ribo
#| fig-cap: Proportion of ribosomal reads detected in each sample.
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5
#tar_read(fig_ribo_prop)
```

## FastQ screen

[FastQ screen](https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastq_screen/) was used to map a sample of reads to several genomes to check for contamination. @fig-fscreen shows one hit one genome percentage. Note, the fill scale is logarithmic with grey indicating zero.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fscreen
#| fig-cap: Fscreen results, one hit per one genome and multiple hits per one genome are inluded.
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 4
#tar_read(fig_fscreen)
```

## Read quality

@fig-read-qual shows read quality as a function of base pair position, @fig-read-qual-clust shows hierarchical clustering based on read quality. This has nothing to do with biology, but rather shows potential batch effects related to sequencing, e.g. different flow cells, different instruments.

```{r}
#| label: fig-read-qual
#| fig-cap: Read quality.
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3
#tar_read(fig_read_qual) 
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-read-qual-clust

#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
#tar_read(fig_read_qual_clust)
```


## Mapping

[STAR](https://github.com/alexdobin/STAR) was used to map reads to the reference genome GRCh38 downloaded from Ensembl (release 111). The following parameters were used:

```         
--outFilterType BySJout 
--outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate
--outFilterMultimapNmax 2
--readFilesCommand zcat
--quantMode GeneCounts
```


## Mapping properties

@fig-star-log and @fig-map-count show mapping summaries.

```{r}
#| label: fig-star-log
#| fig-cap: STAR mapping properties. 
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 10
#tar_read(fig_star_log) 
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-count
#| fig-cap: Input counts vs mapped and counted reads. Samples are ordered from the lowest to the highest percentage of uniquely mapped reads.
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#tar_read(fig_map_count)
```


## Strandedness

Depending on the protocol stranded data can be either way. STAR provides the following in the quantification file:

-   column 2: counts for unstranded RNA-seq
-   column 3: counts for the 1st read strand aligned with RNA
-   column 4: counts for the 2nd read strand aligned with RNA

@fig-star-sense shows the summary of total counts in each column of one example file. Our data are ...

```{r}
#| label: fig-star-sense
#| fig-cap: Distribution of log read count per STAR output file column. The second strand reads are dominant, so we read column 4.
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3
#tar_read(fig_star_sense)
```
